title: Dry-Clean Spend by Garment Type
dataSources: Closet activity (`style:wardrobe`), cleaning tasks (`style:cleaning`), shoe wears (`style:shoes`), beauty inventory (`beauty:product`), audits (`style:audit`).
app: Wardrobe and beauty telemetry — Stylebook closet exports, dry-cleaning reminders, shoe-rotation logs, and makeup inventory audits — streamed to Splunk HEC via exports and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=style:cleaning garment_type=* spend_usd=*
| stats avg(spend_usd) as avg_spend_usd, count as events by garment_type
| sort - avg_spend_usd
description: Shows average dry-clean spend by garment type for cleaning bills.
value: Average dry-clean spend by garment type helps compare cleaning bills across the factors that matter most.
implementation: Capture `spend_usd` on `style:cleaning` events and normalize `garment_type` so Splunk can summarize performance by garment type.
visualization: Bar chart of average dry-clean spend by garment type.
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Splunk Enterprise ≥9.0 or Splunk Cloud — a single-instance home lab is fine. Create `index=personal` with 90–365 day retention (`indexes.conf`).
• **HEC token**: Settings → Data Inputs → HTTP Event Collector → New Token → index `personal`. Store the token in your connector's environment (never commit it to git).
• **Upstream product**: Personal HEC index — HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.
• **Subcategory context**: Wardrobe, Fashion & Beauty — typical feeds: Wardrobe items (`wardrobe:item`), outfit wears (`outfit:wear`), skincare routines (`skincare:routine`), laundry cycles (`laundry:cycle`)..
• **Sourcetypes in this search**: `style:cleaning`.
• **Network**: The connector host must reach both the vendor API/MQTT broker and your Splunk HEC port (8088/tcp).

## Step 1 — Configure data collection

Route **Personal HEC index** events into `index=personal` with `sourcetype=style:cleaning`.

**Collection method:** HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.

**Reference endpoint / path:** `POST https://<splunk>:8088/services/collector/event`.

**Suggested poll interval:** depends on upstream connector.

**Key fields to extract:** `sourcetype-specific — see search filters`.

**Typical connector stack:** Wardrobe and grooming logs — closet apps (Whering, Stylebook), cost-per-wear trackers, skincare-routine logs, and smart-laundry cycles — streamed to Splunk HEC via APIs and scripted inputs..

**Author notes:** Capture `spend_usd` on `style:cleaning` events and normalize `garment_type` so Splunk can summarize performance by garment type.


Example HEC payload shape:

```json
{"index": "personal", "sourcetype": "style:cleaning", "event": { ... vendor fields ... }}
```

Verify ingestion with:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=style:cleaning earliest=-24h | head 20
```

## Step 2 — Create the search and alert

This search implements **Dry-Clean Spend by Garment Type** over `personal` data (primarily `sourcetype=style:cleaning`) across the full search range. The `avg` aggregation groups by `garment_type`; change the `by` clause if you want per-device, per-room, or per-user breakdowns instead.

**Fields this search depends on:** `garment_type`. Confirm each is populated before scheduling alerts.

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=style:cleaning garment_type=* spend_usd=*
| stats avg(spend_usd) as avg_spend_usd, count as events by garment_type
| sort - avg_spend_usd
```

## Step 3 — Validate

**(a) Compare to vendor UI:** Splunk Search → index=personal | stats count by sourcetype. Totals for the same day/week should match within connector lag (usually one poll interval).

**(b) Field presence:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=style:cleaning earliest=-7d
| head 50
| table garment_type
```

Every column the detection uses should be non-null on recent rows.

**(c) Volume sanity:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=style:cleaning earliest=-30d
| timechart span=1d count
```

Flatlines usually mean a broken token, expired OAuth refresh, or HEC URL change.

## Step 4 — Operationalize

Create a companion dashboard titled `UC-25.49.22: Personal evidence` with the following panel layout:

**Panel 1 — Bar Chart Of Average Dry-Clean Spend By Garment Type (the key fields):** Configure according to standard Splunk visualization patterns for this panel type.


Time picker defaults: set to last 30 days with named presets for 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, and 1y — the auditor needs all five windows without retyping. Enable scheduled PDF export for the full dashboard on the regulation's reporting cadence.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting

**Personal HEC index — no Personal HEC index events / missing fields:** If `style:cleaning` stops updating, re-check HEC token, index `personal`, and firewall to port 8088. Search `index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd group=http_event_collector` for rejection reasons. Confirm the Personal HEC index connector script is still running (`systemctl status` or cron log).

**Personal HEC index — NULL values in extracted fields:** The Personal HEC index JSON export shape drifted — compare a raw event (`index=personal sourcetype=style:cleaning | head 1 | spath`) against the field names in Step 2. Re-map in the connector before changing the SPL.

**Personal HEC index — API error / auth denied (401/403):** Refresh tokens expire on most consumer APIs — re-authorize the scripted input, update `passwords.conf` / env vars, and verify the vendor developer app is not in sandbox mode.

**Personal HEC index — endpoint timeout / HTTP 429 throttling:** Back off the poll interval in the connector; Personal HEC index APIs often cap requests per 15 minutes on free tiers.

**Stale dashboard:** Confirm the saved search `dispatch.earliest_time` covers enough history for your `aggregation` buckets.
